newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says to leave Jan prime rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says to leave Jan prime rate unchanged.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd said on Wednesday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for January unchanged at 2.5 percent, a record low.
The prime rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to the long-term credit bank's most creditworthy clients.
IBJ also said it will leave the coupon rate on its January five-year debentures, sold to institutional investors, unchanged from the December issue at 1.6 percent.
The IBJ decision to leave the key lending rate unchanged was in line with the market yield of its 1.6 percent December debenture, which was traded at 1.70 percent this morning, bond traders said.
Japan's long-term prime lending rate is customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon of the benchmark five-year debenture issued monthly by the IBJ.

The other two long-term credit banks -- Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd --are expected to announce their prime lending rates for January and the coupon rates of their January debentures on Thursday.
